key_insight: Phonon Fine-Tuning (PFT) improves machine-learned interatomic potentials by directly supervising second-order derivatives (energy Hessians) so MLIPs reproduce DFT force constants and vibrational properties accurately with a compact fine-tuning step.
problem_solved: Standard MLIP training on energies, forces, and stresses can miss potential-energy curvature, causing large errors in phonons and other vibrational predictions despite low energy/force errors.
method: Compute DFT force constants using finite-displacement phonon calculations for representative structures.
Add a Hessian-level loss that matches the MLIP energy Hessian (second derivatives) to the DFT force-constant matrix and fine-tune the pre-trained MLIP.
Keep original energy/force/stress performance while correcting curvature-driven errors with minimal additional DFT data and training time.
impact: PFT provides a practical plug-in to make MLIPs trustworthy for vibrational, thermal, and stability-sensitive predictions, helping ML practitioners produce physically consistent potentials without retraining from scratch.
visual_elements: Before vs after phonon dispersion plots showing reconstructed phonon bands and reduced errors after PFT
Schematic pipeline: pre-trained MLIP → compute DFT force constants (finite displacements) → Hessian loss → fine-tuned MLIP
Heatmap or matrix comparison of DFT vs MLIP Hessians (force-constant matrices) pre- and post-fine-tuning
Bar chart of error metrics (phonon RMS error, energy/force RMSE) showing preserved energy/force accuracy and reduced curvature error
paper_title: PFT: Phonon Fine-tuning for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
paper_authors: Teddy Koker, Abhijeet Gangan, Mit Kotak, Jaime Marian, Tess Smidt
